v2_1: Your staff are pasting customer data into A I chats. There are three ways to stop it, and each one is good and weak at different things.
v2_2: Nobody is careless; they're fast. One vendor studied about twenty two million enterprise prompts in twenty twenty five, and found around five hundred and eighty thousand sensitive items. Chat G P T accounted for seventy one percent of them.
v2_3: Option one: policy and training. It's cheap, it sets expectations, and you need it anyway. But it depends on memory at the worst moment: a deadline and a chat box.
v2_4: Option two: network tools and gateways. They give central visibility, and can block whole categories of sites. But they see the message after it has left the person's hands, and they have to sit in the middle.
v2_5: Option three: a check at the Send button. It acts before anything leaves, and the person decides. But rules can miss things, and it has to be rolled out on every device and browser.

v2_7: Before you buy anything, ask five questions. Where does the check run: on the device, or on your servers? What do you store, and for how long? What happens when it's unsure? Which apps and browsers does it cover? And can I see the decisions without seeing the text?
